I am one of the two head counselors at a 3 day 2 night camp for children ages 9-17. In previous years, I watched these kids myself, but this year I had some assistance. (Thank God.)

Every year, there's this certain "female" that insists on staying during the nights so she can "help" make breakfast in the staff kitchen.

I could go on about how this lardbeast has to have her way about everything. She has to have her own room, even though we are beyond crowded. She also needs her rest, so she screamed at her 8 year old daughter (who is allowed to stay because the fatty is there) not to bother her over anything. Her daughter is very sweet, funny, and a pretty decent kid.

On day two of camp, my helper came up to me and mentioned that she was 100% sure that the lardbeast's daughter had lice. Helper is taking cosmology classes and said she recognized the pest right away. She understandably wanted me to approach lardbeast about this as we have tons of girls crammed into a small area together for sleeping arrangements.

I approach the lardbeast alone and without mentioning my Helper, I let her know that someone was concerned about her daughter, and maybe she could discreetly check. Now this ham is very dumb, and frequently runs her blood sugar levels amok, but I honestly expected her to take this seriously.

Nope.

I used to be a camper at a summer camp for kids 7-17, and when I was old enough, I worked as a counselor...but the sessions were 2 weeks long. Each session has about 600-800 kids. If a kid had lice (or any other contagious illness), we would quarantine them in the health center until they got better. If it was a serious illness, like Swine Flu (YEAH, that happened one year), we would straight up send them home.

One of the ways that the camp prevents illnesses from coming into the camp is through "health checks" on the way to camp. If kids flew on a plane, health checks were done at the airport. Bus, health checks were done on the bus on the way to camp. If parents drove the kid, health checks were done at the gates. Health checks were quick; they checked the child's hair and temperature. If the kid has lice and/or a fever, they will still let the kid come to camp, but they will immediately quarantine the child when he or she arrives until they are better/ready to interact with everyone.
